### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every trace followed one fixed chain: A21's only observed successor was A22, A22's only observed successor was A23, and the activities A27, A28, A33, A34 and A35 did not occur in any trace. [DIR001, REL001, REL007, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- In the later window, A22 runs in about 57 in 100 traces (113 of 200) instead of all traces, while A27, A28, A33, A34 and A35 each appear in about 43 in 100 traces (87 of 200) after being absent before; none of them repeats within a trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- A21's outgoing flow is redistributed: about 57 in 100 of its observed transitions still go to A22, and the rest go to the new activities (A27 about 10, A28 about 8, A33 about 7, A34 about 8, A35 about 11 per 100). [DIR001]
- In the later window, A22 and each of the five new activities never occur in the same trace, so the two routes are mutually exclusive. [REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]
- The five new activities always run together as one group: every pair of them co-occurs in exactly the about 43 in 100 traces where the group runs, and each pair appears in both orders in similar shares (roughly 18–25 in 100 each way), so there is no fixed order among them. [REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027]
- The group sits between A21 and A23: A21 precedes each group activity in all group traces, and each group activity precedes A23 in all group traces. [REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017]
- From each group activity the flow either continues to another group activity or exits to A23 (exits are about 17–23 in 100 of observed outgoing transitions); A23 still occurs in every trace, after A22 in about 57 in 100 cases and after the group in about 43 in 100. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, REL007]
- The group activities sit around the middle of the trace (mean relative position about 0.52), and A21's relative position moved slightly earlier (mean about 0.49 to about 0.46). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- For context: 45 control-flow items qualified, against roughly 0.49 expected by chance in an unchanged process — far beyond what an unchanged process typically produces. [screening]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that an alternative route between A21 and A23 was introduced alongside the original one. In the later window, in about 43 in 100 cases the flow leaves A21 and passes through the group A27, A28, A33, A34 and A35 — always all five, in varying order — before continuing to A23, bypassing A22; in the remaining about 57 in 100 cases the original A21 → A22 → A23 sequence is retained. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, REL001, REL007, REL008, REL013, REL018]

The supporting signs are that the change is shown directly by directional and relational evidence (A21 now also leads into the group, the group always precedes A23, and A22 and the group never co-occur), the participation figures (about 57 and 43 in 100, with A21 and A23 present throughout) are consistent across the occupancy, direction and relation indicators, and the number of qualifying items (45 against roughly 0.49 expected) far exceeds what random re-splits produce. [DIR001, REL008, REL013, OCC001, screening]

The evidence cannot distinguish a newly inserted alternative within one process from a mixture of two case populations in the later window, and the internal sequencing of the five group activities cannot be pinned down beyond the absence of a fixed pairwise order; zero participation in the earlier window means only that these activities were not observed there. [REL018, OCC002]

Other differences: apart from the slight forward shift in A21's relative position, which is consistent with the new route and not an independent change, the evidence shows no further differences. [POS001]
